issues.legal_issue: A transferee may defend possession obtained in part performance of a contract for sale even after a suit to enforce that contract has become time-barred, if the statutory conditions for protection are met.
material_facts: The transferee took possession of the property in part performance of an agreement to sell.
The agreement was in writing, signed by the transferor, and contained ascertainable terms for the transfer.
The transferee had done acts in furtherance of the agreement and remained ready and willing to perform their part.
The transferee had not brought a suit for specific performance within the limitation period.
The transferor's successor brought a suit to recover possession, and the transferee relied on part performance to defend possession.
issues.conclusion: The expiry of the limitation period for a suit for specific performance does not prevent a transferee who satisfies the required conditions from defending possession under Section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 53-A of the Transfer of Property Act protects a transferee's possession in part performance where there is a contract to transfer immovable property for consideration; the contract is in writing and signed by or on behalf of the transferor; its terms can be ascertained; the transferee took possession in part performance or continued in possession and did an act in furtherance; and the transferee performed or is willing to perform their part. The provision contains no restriction making that defence unavailable merely because a suit for specific performance is time-barred. The Court construed the provision in light of the Special Committee's report and the aims and objects of the 1929 amending Act, relying on R.S. Nayak v. A.R. Antulay for the permissibility of consulting such legislative materials, and approved the view in Mahadeo Nathuji Patil v. Surajbai Khushal Chand Lakkad.

rule.if: transferor_possession_recovery_suit and consideration_contract_for_immovable_property and written_contract_signed_by_transferor and ascertainable_transfer_terms and possession_taken_in_part_performance and act_in_furtherance and performed_or_willing_to_perform and specific_performance_claim_time_barred

predicates.transferor_possession_recovery_suit: A transferor, or a person claiming through the transferor, brought a proceeding to recover possession from the transferee.
predicates.consideration_contract_for_immovable_pro: The parties made a contract for consideration to transfer immovable property.
predicates.written_contract_signed_by_transferor: The transferor, or someone acting on the transferor's behalf, signed a written contract.
predicates.ascertainable_transfer_terms: The written contract states terms from which the intended transfer can be ascertained.
predicates.possession_taken_in_part_performance: The transferee took possession, or continued in possession, in part performance of the contract.
predicates.act_in_furtherance: The transferee did an act in furtherance of the contract.
predicates.performed_or_willing_to_perform: The transferee performed, or was ready and willing to perform, the transferee's part of the contract.
predicates.specific_performance_claim_time_barred: The time for bringing a suit to enforce the contract had expired.

issues.definition: When a transferor seeks possession and the transferee satisfies the stated contract, possession, furtherance, and performance predicates, expiry of the time to enforce the contract does not prevent the transferee from defending that possession.

issues.legal_issue: Expiry of the limitation period for an affirmative claim does not, without an express statutory restriction, bar a defendant from raising a defensive plea.
material_facts: The transferee raised part performance as a defence to a suit seeking recovery of possession.
A suit by the transferee for specific performance of the agreement would have been time-barred.
The transferee sought to protect existing possession through the defence rather than enforce the agreement by an affirmative suit.
issues.conclusion: Limitation bars the remedy of bringing a time-barred suit, but does not by itself extinguish a defence raised in another suit.
issues.legal_principle: The Limitation Act applies to suits and applications and bars the remedy of enforcing a claim through a time-barred action; it does not extinguish a defence unless the law expressly provides otherwise. The Court relied on M.K. Venkatachari v. I.A.R. Arunachalam Pillai, which states that limitation provisions are not to be extended by analogy or logic beyond their terms.

predicates.defendant_raises_defense_in_existing_sui: A defendant raised a plea in a proceeding brought by another party.
predicates.affirmative_claim_time_barred: An affirmative suit to enforce the claim underlying the plea would be time-barred.
predicates.no_express_bar_on_defense: No applicable rule expressly prevents the defendant from raising that plea as a defence.

issues.definition: If a defendant raises a plea in an existing suit, the corresponding affirmative claim is time-barred, and no rule expressly bars the plea, the time bar does not prevent the defence.
